Data licence and attribution

Source: DATA-LICENSE.md

The code of the cvmdata package is released under the MIT licence (see LICENSE.md). The data the package serves is not the package’s own and has a licence of its own.

Source

Every table served by cvmdata originates from the Open Data Portal of the Comissão de Valores Mobiliários (CVM), the Brazilian Securities and Exchange Commission: https://dados.cvm.gov.br/. The package either reads the portal directly (source = "cvm") or reads a mirror of it (source = "mirror", the default).

Licence of the data

The CVM publishes every dataset the package covers under the Open Data Commons Open Database License (ODbL) v1.0: https://opendatacommons.org/licenses/odbl/1-0/. The licence is declared per dataset on the portal (field “Licença” of each dataset page; license_id: odc-odbl in the CKAN API). Checked on 2026-10-24 for the eight datasets the package covers: cia_aberta-cad, cia_aberta-doc-fca, cia_aberta-doc-dfp, cia_aberta-doc-itr, cia_aberta-doc-fre, cia_aberta-doc-cgvn, cia_aberta-doc-vlmo and cia_aberta-doc-ipe.

The mirror is a derivative database

The Parquet files published in this repository’s GitHub Releases (tags mirror-<group>-<dataset>-latest) are produced from the CVM CSV files by the ETL under inst/etl/: the content is the CVM’s, re-encoded (UTF-8), typed according to the CVM’s own data dictionary and partitioned by year. They are a derivative database in the terms of the ODbL and are redistributed under the same licence, ODbL v1.0, as the licence requires.

Attribution for the mirror and for anything you derive from it:

Contains data from the Comissão de Valores Mobiliários (CVM) Open Data Portal, https://dados.cvm.gov.br/, made available under the Open Data Commons Open Database License (ODbL) v1.0. Mirrored and converted to Parquet by the cvmdata R package, https://github.com/SidneyBissoli/cvmdata.

What this means for you

In short (the licence text prevails):

  • You may use, copy, redistribute and adapt the data, including commercially.
  • You must attribute the CVM as the source and keep the licence notice when you redistribute the data or a database derived from it.
  • A database you derive from it and publicly redistribute must be offered under the ODbL as well. Works produced from the data (charts, papers, models, aggregates that are not themselves a database) are not bound by that clause, but must carry the notice.
  • You may not impose technological restrictions on the data beyond those of the licence.

The package does not alter any value published by the CVM. Every tibble it returns carries provenance attributes (source, fetched_at, group, dataset, table, package_version) so that the origin of each result can be audited.
